pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregular polygonal patches with moderate edge angularity and soft pixel gradients. Patch area is largest on the dorsal-lateral flank, transitioning to smaller, more rounded sub-units on the ventral and posterior-limb regions.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Cream-colored interstitial network forming a continuous topological graph. Junction nodes are primarily tri-radial and quadri-radial. Corridor thickness is consistent on the mid-flank (approx. 5-10 pixels at current resolution) but widens into broad, non-geometric fields along the ventral line.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: High-frequency, low-amplitude serrated silhouette along the upper nuchal crest, transitioning to a softer, more diffuse 1D contour toward the withers.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: A notable structural break in the mane continuity is visible at the transition from the upper neck to the shoulder, where the silhouette flattens against the background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Localized area of erythema and textural disruption visible on the upper neck, characterized by a reddened skin surface beneath the beak of a perched avian.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A visible focal wound or skin breach is present on the lateral neck at the site of oxpecker interaction.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of two oxpeckers (Buphagus spp.) on the upper neck/shoulder region, one actively interacting with the dermis.
